input.quote: (c) Upon termination of the Agreement:
input.rationale: The termination-effects provision (para 4(c)) only requires Kubient to cease the Services, revocation of the license, Customer to stop using the platform, and mutual return/destruction of Confidential Information. There is no obligation on Kubient to provide transition assistance, to return AP's data (Requests, Content and related data) in a usable machine-readable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards, and no such language appears elsewhere in the Agreement (no hits for transition, export, migration or Customer Data). For a hosted ad-auction service handling AP data, this absence is a deviation, so we insert the playbook exit provision as new sub-clauses (v)-(vii) of para 4(c): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within thirty days, then deletion with written certification.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The termination-effects provision (para 4(c)) only requires Kubient to cease the Services, revocation of the license, Customer to stop using the platform, and mutual return/destruction of Confidential Information. There is no obligation on Kubient to provide transition assistance, to return AP's data (Requests, Content and related data) in a usable machine-readable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards, and no such language appears elsewhere in the Agreement (no hits for transition, export, migration or Customer Data). For a hosted ad-auction service handling AP data, this absence is a deviation, so we insert the playbook exit provision as new sub-clauses (v)-(vii) of para 4(c): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within thirty days, then deletion with written certification.

p0020: (i) Kubient will cease providing the Services;
p0021: (ii) the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked, (iii) Customer will promptly cease use of the Services and the Auction Platform;

Rendered redline:
p0022: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.
(v) at Customer's request, Kubient will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such termination or expiration at Kubient's then-current rates; (vi) within thirty (30) days of such termination or expiration, Kubient will return to Customer all Requests, Content and other data of or relating to Customer, its Properties, Inventory or Impressions that is in Kubient's possession or control (collectively, "Customer Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (vii) thereafter Kubient will delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

**Final finding: Compliant — no audit right binds us.**

Negotiation note for the file: if Kubient introduces an audit clause, hold it to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Kubient's cost absent underpayment above 5% (fallback: 15 days / 10%), and delete any direct or remote system-access language.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif" and "books" return no hits, and a full read of the Agreement (single section, p0000–p0074) confirms Kubient has no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against The Associated Press and no right of direct or remote access to our systems. The only access obligation on us (p0001) is a cooperation covenant to enable Kubient to deliver the Services, and the fee mechanics in section 5 (p0023) impose no verification right or audit cost-shifting on us; indeed Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits to us, so an "underpayment by Customer" audit mechanic is largely inapposite here. This rule is a protective limitation on Vendor audit rights, so genuine silence leaves us better off than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access). Inserting an audit framework would be counterproductive, implicitly acknowledging an audit right and cost obligation that do not exist today, so no redline is proposed. If Kubient later proposes an audit clause, we should hold it to the preferred parameters and delete any system-access language.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-ip-4a195820","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The Agreement contains no IP or data ownership provision. The only proprietary-rights language is a warranty that Kubient owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and \"products delivered hereunder\" (p0040), a trademark/logo carve-out (p0065), and a clause making AP \"solely liable\" for its Content and the IP rights therein (p0025) without confirming AP owns them. Nothing allocates ownership of deliverables or work product prepared for AP, and nothing addresses AP's data (including Requests sent to Kubient and visitor data Kubient collects and stores under p0035). That leaves the vendor warranty as the only ownership statement touching delivered products and gives AP no licence back to embedded Kubient materials. We therefore added a short IP and data section: AP retains its Content, Properties and data and owns deliverables (Kubient assigns), Kubient keeps the Auction Platform and its pre-existing tools with a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials, Kubient's data use is limited to providing the Services, and no joint ownership is created.","proposal":"Add an IP and data ownership section: AP owns its Content, Properties and data plus deliverables (Kubient assigns), Kubient keeps its platform with a licence back, no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-81a94de8","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 7 contains only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (with indemnification and confidentiality carved out). There is no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement — searches for \"aggregate liability\" and \"exceed\" return nothing, and no cap is hidden in the warranty (para 9) or indemnity (paras 47-55) provisions. Both parties' direct liability is therefore unlimited, leaving Customer's exposure uncapped contrary to the playbook requirement for a meaningful mutual cap. Because the commercial model is revenue share rather than Customer-paid fees, a pure fees-based cap would be illusory, so the cap is drafted as the greater of twelve months' amounts under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped and payment obligations preserved.","proposal":"Add a mutual monetary liability cap (greater of 12 months' amounts and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-e4ff42d6","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Paragraph 8(h) is a mutual assignment clause that already gives AP the key protections: AP may assign without Kubient's consent to any affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all of the relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. The termination provisions (paragraph 4(a)-(b)) are limited to convenience after the Initial Term, material breach and insolvency; there is no change-of-control trigger, no deemed-assignment language and no Kubient right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control, so none of the walk-away conditions are present. This meets the playbook fallback (mutual assignment with successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard for other assignments); pressing for the asymmetric preferred formulation (Kubient consent-only plus a competitor bar) would be disproportionate given the balanced bargain already struck, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-5974860c","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 1 (Kubient Services) expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms AP remains free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties, which matches our preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer. Searches for \"exclusiv\", \"sole\", \"minimum\" and requirements/third-party restriction patterns surface no covenant binding AP to deal only with Kubient: the other \"exclusive\" references are a non-exclusive license grant to AP (p0002), exclusive jurisdiction (p0064), each Party's own trademark ownership (p0065), the entire-agreement clause (p0072) and the no-third-party-beneficiary clause (p0073). There is also no minimum volume or non-compete commitment (p0014, p0062 confirm no revenue guarantee). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-f0e77df4","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"No liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee amount is payable by AP anywhere in the Agreement. Section 5 is a pure revenue-share (Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits AP's share, with AP owing only applicable transaction taxes), so there are no committed subscription fees that could be accelerated. The only termination-related payment language (Section 4(a)) entitles Kubient to fees actually \"generated during the termination period\" — i.e., its share of revenue genuinely earned during the 90-day notice period — which is compensation for value received, not a fixed sum payable by AP as liquidated damages or a penalty. Section 7(a) also bars punitive damages against either Party. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2b2c9cd1","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The grant in paragraph 2 runs to \"Customer\" only, with no coverage for AP affiliates or contractors acting on AP's behalf and no path to add them, and it is expressly \"non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense\" and \"revocable\". As drafted the licence is revocable at Kubient's discretion at any time during the Term, which sits at the playbook walk-away line; the separate revocation on termination in paragraph 4(c)(ii) is acceptable but the unqualified \"revocable\" is not. The non-transferability also conflicts with paragraph 8(h), which permits assignment to an affiliate, asset purchaser or successor by merger. Redline extends the grant to affiliates and contractors, makes it sublicensable and transferable to permitted successors, and limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4.","proposal":"Extend platform licence to AP affiliates and contractors, permit successor transfer, and remove revocability at will.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-eaa37113","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Searches for exclusivity, competition, restriction, solicitation and \"Customer shall/will not\" language surface no non-compete, field-of-use or territory covenant binding AP. Clause 1 (p0001) expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms AP remains free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. The only Customer prohibitions (p0025) are ordinary license-scope and IP protections (no transfer, third-party access, reverse engineering, resale or service-bureau use of Kubient's Service) rather than restraints on AP's businesses, purchases or internal development. This falls short of the preferred position (Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) and is a missing-behaviour deviation for a term that rolls beyond 12 months. The clause is also symmetrical, giving Kubient a walk-away right on 90 days' notice at any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a term. The redline adds a 30-day AP convenience right with refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, and confines Kubient's convenience right to the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice; the 60-90 day fallback is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Add AP a 30-day termination-for-convenience right with refund of prepaid fees; limit Kubient's convenience right to end of term on 90 days' notice.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-898c0902","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 14(a) selects Delaware law (fallback-only) while fixing venue in New York courts, so law and forum are mismatched. Our preferred position is New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is achieved by a one-word substitution while leaving the venue sentence otherwise intact. Venue is already domestic courts and the Section 8 AAA arbitration clause has no foreign seat, so no walk-away trigger; we flag the arbitration/exclusive-venue conflict in the comment only rather than expanding the redline.","proposal":"Change governing law from Delaware to New York and confirm New York County venue.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-6f5e2bd0","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or price/terms-matching obligation in either direction. Searches for \"most favored nation\", \"favorable\", \"no less favorable\", \"best price\" and third-party term-matching language returned no results, and the only commercial terms provision (§5 Fees and Payment, p0023) is a simple revenue-share deferred to the Exhibits with no MFN or benchmarking mechanic. Section 1 (p0001) further confirms the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from offering Inventory via other agents or selling to third parties, so AP is under no obligation to extend Kubient terms given to others. This matches the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer); no redline is warranted. Note for diligence: MFN risk could still be introduced in an Exhibit, which should be checked when Exhibits are negotiated.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-e8d9948e","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The economics are a pure revenue share: under Section 5 AP owes no fees at all (Kubient pays AP a share of revenue actually generated), and there is no minimum spend, volume floor, shortfall charge or take-or-pay obligation anywhere in the Agreement. Section 1 expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP may offer Inventory through other agents or sell it to third parties, so there is no volume restriction on AP either. The only \"minimum\" references are the Customer-set floor price in the Winning Bid Price definition (p0014, a protection for us) and the disclaimer that no minimum revenue level is guaranteed (p0062) — neither imposes a purchase commitment on us. Section 4(a) locks the Initial Term to one year absent breach, but with no committed spend that creates no take-or-pay exposure, so the preferred position (\"no minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only\") is met and no redline is needed. Note for the deal team: any Exhibit added later should be checked for minimum spend or volume floors.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-aa678cbd","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"No non-solicit clause exists, so the sub-checks for duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable rather than failed. Searches for \"solicit\", \"non-solicitation\", \"hire\", \"employ or engage\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"poach\", \"personnel\" and \"directly or indirectly\" return no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere in the agreement. The only employment-adjacent provisions are the independent contractor/no-agency clause quoted above (p0066), the mutual indemnities (p0051/p0052) and confidentiality handling by employees (p0061); none restricts either party from soliciting or hiring the other's personnel. Our preferred NOSOLICIT position is that no non-solicit bind the Customer, and that position is met by this absence, so no redline and no counterparty comment are warranted and the paragraph stands unchanged. Internal note only, not to be raised with Kubient: if Kubient later proposes a non-solicit, we would require it to be mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, capped at 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and with no \"no-hire\".","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-5c736b12","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Paragraph 4(a) provides indefinite automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanism: the only exit is a for-convenience termination on ninety (90) days' written notice available only after the Initial Term, so Customer's effective opt-out window is 90 days — at the walk-away boundary and well beyond the preferred 30 days (fallback 60 days). There is also no vendor renewal reminder. Renewal term length (12 months) is compliant, and the revenue-share fee model in paragraph 5 contains no price-uplift language, so no uplift cap is needed. Redline adds a 30-day Customer non-renewal right and a 60-day Kubient reminder while leaving the existing termination rights untouched.","proposal":"Add 30-day Customer non-renewal right and 60-day vendor renewal reminder to the auto-renewing 1-year term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-0f780f51","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The termination-effects provision (para 4(c)) only requires Kubient to cease the Services, revocation of the license, Customer to stop using the platform, and mutual return/destruction of Confidential Information. The Section 13 disclaimer does carve out the express warranties (\"Except as expressly set forth herein ... except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement\"), so it does not swallow them; the gap is duration and remedy. We insert the missing warranty, period and remedy after p0041 as new clauses (xii)-(xiii) of Section 9(b), the smallest edit reaching the preferred position, with the 90-day fallback offered in the comment.","proposal":"Add a workmanlike performance warranty, a conformance warranty period and a repair/replace/refund remedy to Kubient's warranties","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-e0ac58d2","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"low","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Searches for \"audit\", \"inspect\", \"records\", \"verif\" and \"books\" return no hits, and a full read of the Agreement (single section, p0000–p0074) confirms Kubient has no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against The Associated Press and no right of direct or remote access to our systems. The only access obligation on us (p0001) is a cooperation covenant to enable Kubient to deliver the Services, and the fee mechanics in section 5 (p0023) impose no verification right or audit cost-shifting on us; indeed Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits to us, so an \"underpayment by Customer\" audit mechanic is largely inapposite here. This rule is a protective limitation on Vendor audit rights, so genuine silence leaves us better off than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access). Inserting an audit framework would be counterproductive, implicitly acknowledging an audit right and cost obligation that do not exist today, so no redline is proposed. If Kubient later proposes an audit clause, we should hold it to the preferred parameters and delete any system-access language.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-indemn-7da45b86","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side indemnity in our favour (Services, Auction Platform, breach of representation or warranty, Kubient's and its subcontractors' acts or omissions), Section 11 supplies standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the damages limitation so the indemnity is uncapped. However, the enumerated prongs (p0048-p0051) contain no express intellectual-property infringement trigger, nor express breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data incident or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers. IP claims are reached only indirectly, via the broad \"Services\"/\"Auction Platform\" wording or by first proving breach of the Section 9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty (p0033) - a route that lets Kubient argue an IP claim is outside the indemnity or requires proof of warranty breach before defence is owed. The playbook requires the provider to stand behind third-party IP claims on the face of the indemnity, so we add an express prong (vi) for IP infringement plus (vii) breach of Law, (viii) Kubient-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, and (ix) gross negligence or wilful misconduct. This is a clarifying addition consistent with warranties Kubient has already given (p0033, p0035, p0037, p0041) and should be uncontroversial; if Kubient resists, our fallback is the IP prong alone with the usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. Spot-check on the reciprocal side: AP's Section 10(b) indemnity (p0052) runs wider than the preferred \"Customer content / Customer breach of law\" limit, extending to AP's unauthorised or inappropriate use of the Services and Auction Platform, breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of AP and its contractors; we have left it untouched because it mirrors Kubient's own prongs and reopening it would invite reciprocal narrowing of the Vendor indemnity we are strengthening.","proposal":"Add express IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct prongs to Kubient's Section 10(a) indemnity.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-51d7c821","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The Agreement has no insurance clause anywhere (searches for \"insurance\" return nothing; General Provisions in p0064-p0073 cover governing law, publicity, notices, force majeure and assignment only). Kubient is a services/hosting vendor that hosts the Auction Platform and, per its own warranty in p0035, collects, maintains and stores visitor information (data), so the playbook's preferred coverages apply. We inserted a new Section 14(j) requiring CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, professional (E&O) liability of USD 2M, cyber/privacy liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request; the fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is available if Kubient pushes back. The obligation binds the counterparty only.","proposal":"Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber) as new Section 14(j)","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**Client:** The Associated Press ("AP", Customer) | **Counterparty:** Kubient (Vendor) | **Document:** Master Services Agreement dated 5 February

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **two critical gaps, four high/medium deviations, three missing protections, and two items requiring internal verification**. The commercial structure is favourable in several respects: the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive, there is no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no Customer-payable liquidated damages, no non-solicit and no Vendor audit right against us, and the mutual assignment clause already carries the successor and affiliate carve-outs we need. We recommend leaving those provisions untouched.

The principal exposures are:

- **No liability cap anywhere in the Agreement.** Section 7 excludes indirect and consequential damages only; direct liability on both sides is unlimited. Because the model is revenue share rather than Customer-paid fees, we have proposed a cap drafted as the greater of twelve months' amounts and USD 1,000,000, with the usual uncapped Excluded Claims.
- **No IP or data ownership provision.** The only ownership language is a Vendor warranty that Kubient owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and "products delivered hereunder". Nothing allocates deliverables or work product to AP, and nothing addresses AP's data, including visitor data Kubient collects and stores under its own warranty.
- **Licence grant is revocable at will** and runs to "Customer" alone, with no affiliate, contractor, sublicence or successor coverage — and it conflicts with the assignment clause that permits transfer to an affiliate, asset purchaser or successor.
- **Lock-in.** No Customer termination for convenience during the Initial Term, indefinite one-year auto-renewals, and a 90-day opt-out available only after the Initial Term.
- **No exit mechanics, no insurance covenant, and gaps in the warranty and indemnity architecture** (no express IP infringement prong; no warranty period or remedy).

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble | No IP or data ownership provision. We add: AP retains its Content, Properties and data and owns deliverables (Kubient assigns); Kubient keeps the Auction Platform and pre-existing tools with a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials; Kubient's data use limited to providing the Services; no joint ownership. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | Preamble | No monetary cap in the Agreement; direct liability is unlimited. We add a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' amounts and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped and payment obligations preserved. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble | Grant is "revocable", non-transferable and non-sublicensable, and runs to Customer only. We extend it to AP affiliates and contractors, permit transfer to permitted successors, and confine revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Preamble | No AP convenience right during the Initial Term; Kubient may exit on 90 days' notice at any time after it. We add a 30-day AP convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, and confine Kubient's right to the end of the then-current Term. Fallback: 60–90 days. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble | Mutual clause already permits AP assignment to affiliates, asset purchasers and successors, with reasonableness for other assignments; no change-of-control trigger or re-pricing right. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | Preamble | Exclusivity expressly disclaimed; AP remains free to use other agents or sell to third parties. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restraint on AP; Customer prohibitions are ordinary licence-scope and IP protections. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | Preamble | Pure revenue share; no penalty, minimum fee or acceleration payable by AP. Termination-period fees reflect revenue actually earned. No redline. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Preamble | Vendor warranties omit a workmanlike-performance warranty, any conformance warranty period, and any remedy. We add these as new clauses of the warranty section; 90-day fallback offered in comment. The general disclaimer carves out express warranties, so it does not swallow them. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | Preamble | Indefinite one-year auto-renewals with a 90-day post-Initial-Term exit as the only opt-out and no renewal reminder. We add a 30-day AP non-renewal right and a 60-day Kubient reminder. Renewal term length and absence of price uplift are compliant. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | Preamble | Termination effects address only cessation, licence revocation and return of Confidential Information. We add six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in a usable machine-readable format within thirty days, then deletion with written certification. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Preamble | Delaware law (fallback-only) is paired with New York venue. We substitute New York law and confirm New York County venue. We flag the arbitration/exclusive-venue tension in comment only. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN, benchmarking or terms-matching obligation in either direction. No redline. Confirm when Exhibits are negotiated. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | Preamble | No minimum spend, volume floor, shortfall charge or take-or-pay; AP owes no fees under the revenue-share model. No redline. Confirm when Exhibits are negotiated. |
